rulings.challenge_claim: The row's claim that Eccl.7.9 shares "no repeated phrase" with the double tov-saying before it is contradicted by the shared root ruach, which closes 7:8 twice and opens 7:9's own clause.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: the רוח (ruach) skeleton sweep returns 20 verses book-wide; restricted to ch.7 it returns exactly the two consecutive verses 7:8 and 7:9 (oshb:Eccl.7.8 “ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ רֽוּחַ”, byte tier; oshb:Eccl.7.9 “בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖”, byte tier). The row's boundary_rationale states the verse shares “no repeated phrase” with 7:8, but the byte-true lexeme recurs at the row's own front seam undisclosed, which the standing cross-seam-cohesion rule treats as arguing continuity unless disclosed. The atomic single_saying call itself plausibly survives: ruach carries two different senses across the seam (7:8's patience/pride idiom vs. 7:9's temperament sense), with no grammatical dependency comparable to the 7:11-7:12 causal clause, so no merge is warranted — but the stated warrant overclaims a total absence of shared vocabulary.
rulings.remedy: Revise the boundary_rationale/device_notes at p02-017 to disclose the ruach-root recurrence rather than deny it, e.g.: the verse repeats the ruach root of 7:8's idiom (in the different, temperament sense) at its own opening, a byte-true lexical echo across the row's front seam (sweep: 2 of the 20 book-wide ruach-root verses fall in ch.7, both consecutive: 7:8-7:9); disclosed as texture, not merge-grade cohesion, because the two verses apply the root to unrelated senses with no grammatical dependency. Test the cure must pass: the revised field must name the shared root and the sweep digit rather than asserting its absence.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's opening-seam denial suppresses the chapter's only contiguous ruach catchword pair, and its cross-row root note cites the divergent site while omitting the identical-form one.
rulings.grounds: Two distinct byte-confirmed defects. (1) Convergent with the LF item on this row — same underlying defect, not a distinct one: the ch.7-scoped רוח sweep returns exactly the contiguous pair 7:8, 7:9 (book-wide 20). (2) Distinct, independently confirmed: the בהל (be-hasty) root sweeps to exactly 3 verses book-wide — oshb:Eccl.5.1 (=web:Eccl.5.2), oshb:Eccl.7.9, oshb:Eccl.8.3. Byte comparison of the source forms shows oshb:Eccl.5.1 “תְּבַהֵ֨ל” and the row's own oshb:Eccl.7.9 “תְּבַהֵ֥ל” share the identical piel stem, while oshb:Eccl.8.3 “תִּבָּהֵ֤ל” is nifal — a different stem, matching the row's own characterization of 8:3. But device_notes names only the divergent-stem site (8:3) as the cross-row echo and omits the closer, same-stem match, which additionally sits in the offset zone (MT 5:1 = WEB 5:2). A cross-row echo note that cites the weaker parallel while dropping the stronger, offset-zone one is a citation-completeness defect.
rulings.remedy: (1) Same remedy as the LF ruling on this row: disclose the ruach-root recurrence at the front seam. (2) Correct device_notes' בהל cross-row note to name both attested recurrences and their stems — the same-stem exact match at oshb:Eccl.5.1 (=web:Eccl.5.2, offset zone, dual-cited per the book's own offset-zone rule) and the different-stem (nifal) recurrence at oshb:Eccl.8.3 — rather than citing only the latter. Test the cure must pass: a rerun of the בהל sweep must show the revised note names all 3 book-wide sites (or explicitly and correctly scopes to fewer with a stated reason), not a single cherry-picked one.

rulings.challenge_claim: device_notes states that 7:10 anticipates the 7:11-7:12 wisdom sayings "without sharing their vocabulary," but 7:10's own prefixed form repeats the chokmah root that opens 7:11 and recurs twice in 7:12.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: the חכמה (wisdom, noun) skeleton sweep returns 22 verses book-wide including a contiguous three-verse run at oshb:Eccl.7.10 “מֵחָכְמָ֖ה”, oshb:Eccl.7.11 “חָכְמָ֖ה”, oshb:Eccl.7.12 “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה” ... “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה” (byte tier throughout). device_notes' claim that 7:10 anticipates 7:11-7:12 “without sharing their vocabulary” is byte-false — the identical root closes 7:10 and opens 7:11.
rulings.remedy: See the combined remedy under the OL ruling for this row (same cure applies to both items).

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's explicit statement that this verse anticipates the following pair "without sharing their vocabulary" is refuted by its own bytes: the wisdom lexeme is shared straight across the row's closing seam.
rulings.grounds: Same core defect as the LF item (convergent, byte-false vocabulary-absence claim), confirmed by both a narrower noun-only sweep (חכמה skeleton: 22 book-wide, 7:10-7:12 contiguous) and, independently, a broader root-family sweep that accounts for the final/medial-mem allography hazard (medial-mem חכמ substring: 32 book-wide; ch.7 members 7:4, 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:19, 7:23, 7:25 — matching OL's digit exactly). Two further defects, independently confirmed, beyond the LF item: (a) internal inconsistency — the very next row (p02-019) offers the identical root at identical strength as its own merge-grade cohesion evidence for 7:11-7:12, while this row denies the root's presence at its own boundary one clause earlier; the evidentiary standard is applied inconsistently across adjacent rows of the same cluster. (b) device_notes' claim “No tov-opener or refrain tag” is true only of the verse-initial slot (7:10 is absent from the staged 12-site tov_openers inventory), but the verse independently carries an inflected tov-min adjacency, “הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה” (‘were better than these,’ byte tier), which escapes the staged 6-verse tov_min_adjacent inventory (3:22, 4:3, 4:6, 6:3, 6:9, 9:4) because it is plural-inflected (טובים vs. the singular טוב/טובה the inventory's skeleton token matches) — an undisclosed instance of the chapter's own better-than texture, matching the toolkit's own flagged tov-מ phrase-extension hazard.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite device_notes at p02-018 to (1) disclose the shared root — the verse's own wisdom-critique close carries the same root the immediately following wisdom-value sayings use as merge-grade cohesion (sweep: root family 7 of 32 book-wide occurrences fall in ch.7, a contiguous chain at 7:10-7:12), disclosed as cross-seam texture and not treated as binding here because 7:10 is a complete self-standing rebuke with no grammatical dependency on 7:11, unlike 7:12's dependency on 7:11; (2) disclose the inflected tov-min construction as texture, noting it is not one of the 6 canonical tov-min-adjacent sites (plural inflection) and not one of the 12 tov-openers (verse-initial token is אל, not tov). Test the cure must pass: the revised device_notes must not assert absence of a root/construction that a ch.7-scoped sweep confirms present at the row's own seam, and the ‘shared vocabulary’ evidentiary standard must be applied the same way at p02-018 and p02-019.

rulings.challenge_claim: The saying_cluster's own front-seam claim -- that 7:11 is held apart from 7:10 on "no shared vocabulary" -- is contradicted by the very root (chokmah, "wisdom") the row treats as its cluster's binding term.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed by the same חכמה sweep as the p02-018 ruling (22 book-wide, contiguous 7:10-7:12, byte tier). The internal 7:11|7:12 grammatical dependency (the כי-clause) is byte-sound and the saying_cluster call plausibly survives on that basis; the challenge to the row's OWN opening-seam denial against 7:10 is correct.
rulings.remedy: See the combined remedy under the OL ruling for this row (same cure applies to both items).

rulings.challenge_claim: The internal merge is byte-sound and the offset-zone crosswalk checks out, but the row's opening-seam denial of shared vocabulary is byte-false and one cited Hebrew form is below quotation tier.
rulings.grounds: Convergent core defect confirmed (same underlying root chain as the LF item). Two further defects independently confirmed on re-derivation: (1) re-collating the row's own cited particle, spliced byte-for-byte from the row's boundary_rationale (“כִּי”), against oshb:Eccl.7.12 returns tier=accent_stripped, not byte — confirmed by direct re-collation (source form “כִּ֛י”). A hand-typed pointed run below quotation grade, uncited as to tier, used to support a boundary-relevant grammatical claim. Re-derivation surfaces a related, further defect beyond what OL raised: the row's own central shared-root claim — “share the root חכמה” — cites that root in bare, unpointed consonants with no diacritics at all; re-collating this bare string against the oshb:Eccl.7.11-Eccl.7.12 window returns tier=skeleton, an even lower grade than the particle OL flagged, for the row's single most load-bearing Hebrew claim (new finding). (2) The row's first verse ends on “לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ”, one of the toolkit's own 5 documented bare-shemesh sites outside the tachat-hashemesh formula (1:5, 6:5, 7:11, 11:7, 12:2) — correctly not claimed as the refrain, but undisclosed as texture, and the same ראה root recurs as the imperative at oshb:Eccl.7.13 “רְאֵ֖ה” and oshb:Eccl.7.14 “רְאֵ֑ה” immediately past this row's own closing seam (also relevant to the p02-020/p02-021 rulings below).
rulings.remedy: (1) Same core remedy as p02-018: rewrite the opening-seam denial to disclose the shared root rather than deny it (the internal 7:11|7:12 merge argument does not require denying a relation to 7:10). (2) Re-splice both the כי particle and the חכמה root mention from verse_map_oshb.json at byte tier with an inline oshb: ref and explicit tier label, per the standing pointed-splice-plus-tier-label rule; do not hand-type either. (3) Optionally disclose the “לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ” / imperative-ראה echo at the closing seam as texture. Test the cure must pass: re-run the collator against the revised field and confirm tier=byte for both Hebrew claims.

rulings.challenge_claim: The pair's binding evidence sits outside every quoted run, the second quote overruns its own gloss by one token, and the closing seam carries an undisclosed same-root straddle.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed against the full verse text. The row's byte-tier Hebrew quote of oshb:Eccl.7.14 stops at “רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם”, omitting the remainder of the verse including “עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים” — the very token the row's own rationale names as shared binding evidence (‘share the root עשה ... with ha-elohim as referent’). The paired WEB quote stops at ‘consider,’ one token short of rendering ‘yes/also’ which the Hebrew quote does include — a quote/gloss parity break. The subject description is also imprecise: in oshb:Eccl.7.13 “מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים” is a construct chain (ha-elohim as nomen rectum, not a verbal subject); only 7:14's “עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים” has ha-elohim as verbal subject — the row's phrasing does not distinguish the two. The עשה root is confirmed not seam-exclusive: a skeleton sweep returns exactly 4 ch.7 verses — 7:13, 7:14, 7:20, 7:29 — and 7:20 falls inside this same cluster's own p02-024 row, an undisclosed cross-row recurrence. The closing-seam claim is also confirmed: the row's own “רְאֵ֑ה” (7:14) is answered by “רָאִ֖יתִי” (7:15, same root), and the resh-ayin pair “רָעָ֖ה” (7:14) / “בְּרָעָתֽוֹ” (7:15) is confirmed as 2 of the 3 ch.7 members of that skeleton sweep, correctly treated by OL as distinct senses (calamity vs. evildoing), not blended. Independently confirmed strongest tie the row omits: both 7:13 and 7:14 use the DEFINITE divine form האלהים, part of the inventory's 28-verse definite set (vs. 7 bare) — the more precise, available evidence for exactly the pairing the row argues, left uncited.
rulings.remedy: (1) Extend the byte-tier Hebrew quote of oshb:Eccl.7.14 through “עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים” so the quoted span actually contains the token doing the cited work, and extend the WEB gloss to the matching content point (quote/gloss parity repair, one edit). (2) Correct the subject description to distinguish the construct chain at 7:13 from the verbal subject at 7:14. (3) Cite the definite-form (ha-elohim) tie explicitly as the pairing's own strongest textual evidence, with the 28/7 sweep digit. (4) Disclose the עשה recurrence at 7:20 and the ראה/רעה recurrences across the 7:14|7:15 seam as texture. Test the cure must pass: re-run the quote/gloss parity check and confirm the Hebrew and WEB quoted spans end at the same content point, and confirm the binding-evidence token sits inside the quoted byte-tier run rather than only being named in prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: The verse is isolated on a register shift while four byte-true lexical chains straddle its two seams undisclosed, and the hevel-family token inside its own bytes is not disclosed at all.
rulings.grounds: All four cross-seam chains and the hevel token are byte-confirmed. Opening seam: “רָאִ֖יתִי” (7:15) and “רְאֵ֑ה” (7:14) share the ראה root — the same root the p02-020 ruling above also flags as undisclosed at this identical seam (same underlying defect viewed from both adjoining rows, not two separate defects); “בְּרָעָתֽוֹ” answers “רָעָ֖ה” (resh-ayin sweep, ch.7: 7:3, 7:14, 7:15, correctly split calamity/evildoing, not blended). Closing seam: a skeleton sweep of צדיק (the correct attested spelling, with the mater lectionis yod) returns exactly 3 ch.7 verses — 7:15, 7:16, 7:20 — and of רשע exactly 3 — 7:15, 7:17, 7:25 — confirming both paradox-nouns of 7:15 (“צַדִּיק֙”, “רָשָׁ֔ע”) recur in the very verses of the following row (p02-022's span 7:16-7:18: “צַדִּיק֙” at 7:16, “תִּרְשַׁ֥ע” at 7:17). The row argues this relation only in English (‘the counsel responds to’) without disclosing it as byte-true shared lexemes. The hevel-family claim is independently confirmed: “בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י” carries the suffixed hevel form, one of only 2 ch.7 hevel-family tokens (the other at 7:6, within the family's book-wide 30-verse/38-token count), and the toolkit's own suffixed-form inventory lists this spelling as a single book occurrence — undisclosed in observed_substrate_signals, which name only the I-saw frame (that citation is itself correct and independently re-verified: 7:15 is among the 18-verse raiti inventory).
rulings.remedy: Disclose all four cross-seam chains and the hevel token as texture in device_notes/observed_substrate_signals: the ראה-root echo answering 7:14's imperative, the resh-ayin calamity/evildoing pair (objects named, not blended), the צדיק/רשע paradox-noun recurrence into the following row's span (7:16-7:18), and the sole-occurrence suffixed hevel form (2 of 2 ch.7 hevel tokens). None of these require moving the row's own seams — the register shift from first-person report to second-person imperative remains a clean, independently sufficient basis for both boundaries — the defect is non-disclosure of byte-true cross-seam continuity signals, per the standing cross-seam-cohesion rule. Test the cure must pass: a symmetry check of this cluster's disclosed cross-row echoes must show 7:15's paradox nouns and hevel token named at least once (in this row or a neighbor), not asserted as isolated.
